overall_cpt_analysis.summary: Overall CPT quality is poor. While the evaluated CPTs are structurally valid and normalized, most node-level verdicts are poor due to substantial parameter mismatch from the reference. Specifically, 5 of 7 nodes are rated poor, 2 are fair, and only 1 is excellent, so the network is dominated by inaccurate CPT parameterization rather than isolated issues.
main_reasons: Most evaluated nodes received poor verdicts: Deviation_in_Dispatch, Deviation_in_Response, Network_Manipulation, and Root_Causes show substantial parameter inaccuracies.
The poor nodes have high mean absolute errors, often around 0.25 to 0.30, with very large maximum errors up to 0.88.
Several nodes contain many severe parameter deviations, including 20 severe errors for Deviation_in_Dispatch, 24 for Deviation_in_Response, and 14 for Root_Causes.
Only Program_Anomaly is excellent, while Execution_Integrity and Physical_Anomaly are merely fair, which is not enough to offset the majority of poor CPTs.
The dominant issue is parameter inaccuracy, not CPT validity, since the node-level analyses indicate the tables are well-formed but often far from ground truth.
